text:
sarah: Heads-up — after last release we got a surge of reports around the onboarding flow: users failing to complete step 3. Also a few customers requested a small CTA tweak. Need to decide bug-first vs polish for the next mini-sprint. Thoughts?
triage-bot: New issue #4752 created by Acme Corp - reproduction steps + console logs attached. Severity: P2. Affects ~12% of onboarding sessions in the last 24h. https://issues.internal/4752 :rotating_light:
leon: Can we reproduce reliably? If it's hitting 12% of sessions I'd lean towards moving the bug into the top of the hotfix slice. @maya any estimate on dev time?
maya: Reproduced locally. Root cause looks like a race in the async payload handler when network latency spikes. Quick patch should be ~4-6 dev hours + test & canary. Low risk. The CTA copy/design polish is separate and probably 2-3 dev hours but design wants to iterate.
devon: CS says customer would accept a quick copy change immediately as mitigation. They prefer function over polish for now. We could ship the bug fix and do copy + A/B in next minor.
sarah: Proposal: ship the bug fix in the hotfix (canary tomorrow morning), include the copy tweak as a follow-on enhancement in the next minor release. If the canary shows regressions, auto-rollback and escalate. Agree?
leon: :thumbsup: agree. I'll own the hotfix rollout and coordinate QA smoke tests.
maya: I'll open the PR now and tag @eng-oncall and QA. ETA: PR by EOD, patch ready for canary tomorrow.
triage-bot: Issue #4752 added to sprint 'hotfix-2026-03-23' and assigned to leon. Linked PR: git://rwd/patch/4752 (status: open).
devon: One more ask — can we add a short-term metric alert for onboarding failures so we spot recurrences quickly? @sam from eng-sre
sam: On it. I'll add an onboarding_error_rate alert (threshold: >1% over 5m) and a brief runbook that points to the hotfix and rollback steps.
sarah: Great. We'll coordinate customer comms after canary. @maya include the unit/integration test links in the PR description and ping here when canary starts. Thanks everyone.
